_comment: The last EAS build that actually shipped this app, recorded so CI can
tell when mobile/ has drifted ahead of what anyone can install.
This exists because on 2026-08-21 the installed app turned out to be
three days and eleven commits stale. The share button the owner was
looking for had never been in a build. Nothing surfaced that: CI
typechecks mobile/ but has never built it, and the API deploys on every
merge, so the two halves drifted apart silently.
Update it by running `node scripts/record-eas-build.mjs` from mobile/
AFTER a build finishes. It reads the real build from EAS rather than
taking your word for it.
Not authoritative, and honest about that: nothing stops a human editing
this file without building. Adding an EXPO_TOKEN secret would let the
CI job query EAS directly and remove that gap — see the job's own
comment in .github/workflows/ci-cd.yml.
A platform may carry `buildsUnavailableUntil` (a date) and
`buildsUnavailableReason`. While that date is in the future, CI
reports its drift as a warning instead of failing — because a
platform that CANNOT be built has no action behind a red check,
and permanent red is exactly what taught everyone to ignore
expo-doctor.
It expires by itself. Past the date the exemption stops applying
and the check fails again with nobody doing anything, so this
cannot rot into a permanent mute — which would be worse than the
red it replaces, because it would fail silently.

IOS.buildsUnavailableReason: EAS free-plan iOS build quota exhausted; resets 1 September
